longForm.overview:
🫁 is the emoji of breath-coded 'catch-a-breath' lung reveal — a pair of anatomical human lungs shown front-facing with bronchi and trachea visible, the iconography of breath-coded catch-your-breath, lung-health-coded awareness, and the universal 'I cannot breathe' tag. Where 👃 reads as nose-coded smell flex and 🫀 reads as anatomical-heart-coded pulse moment, 🫁 captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate breath-coded energy — a 'I cannot breathe 🫁' catch-a-breath-coded check-in or a 'lung health matters 🫁' breath-coded reveal. The paired-lungs-with-bronchi visual cue borrows from the universal anatomy-textbook tradition and the modern respiratory-health aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as breath-coded rather than literal lungs.

In real-world usage 🫁 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate respiratory-coded catch-your-breath. A partner sends it on a 'I cannot breathe 🫁' breath-coded check-in. A friend sends it on a 'lung health matters 🫁' respiratory-coded reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'take a deep breath 🫁' catch-a-breath-coded message. The paired-lungs-with-bronchi visual cue is what makes the emoji feel breath-coded — it is not just 'lungs,' it is 'catch-a-breath-coded respiratory flex.'

What separates 🫁 from the rest of the body-parts family is the catch-a-breath-coded register. The emoji is not saying 'nose smelling' (👃), 'heart pulse' (🫀), or 'tongue taste' (👅). It is saying 'breath-coded catch-a-breath,' which carries a specific respiratory-health tradition. That is why 🫁 travels especially well on respiratory-coded reveals, breath-coded check-ins, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with catch-a-breath-coded energy.

In group chats 🫁 anchors 'breath moment' threads, respiratory-coded reveals, and 'take a deep breath 🫁' coded moments where the paired-lungs-with-bronchi visual cue matches the register. On Instagram it lands on breath-coded flat-lays and lung-health-coded stories. On TikTok it travels in respiratory-coded transitions and 'I cannot breathe' reaction content.

The emoji also works in dating contexts. A 'take a deep breath tonight 🫁' partner message uses the paired-lungs-with-bronchi visual cue to communicate breath-coded soft-coded romance. Across all of these surfaces the rule is the same: the more respiratory-coded the moment, the more natural 🫁 feels.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip 🫁 in sympathy, condolence, or break-up contexts. The breath-coded catch-a-breath cue is the wrong tone for any conversation where the moment is somber. A quiet ❤️ or a sentence that acknowledges the moment is a better fit.

Avoid 🫁 in pure celebration or hype-coded moments where the respiratory-coded rule feels off. A 'take a deep breath 🫁' message works for breath-coded reveal; for hype-coded celebrations use 🙌 or a sentence.

Skip 🫁 when you want to communicate pulse-coded heartbeat. The breath-coded register is too catch-a-breath for heart-pulse moments; use 🫀 when the heartbeat-coded read needs to land clean.
